# CryptoEngine — portfolio case study by Hisashi Aoki

> A 24/7 event-driven trading and execution platform built for deterministic state,
> fail-safe operation and low-footprint deployment. Public, sanitized portfolio snapshot
> with live execution disabled by default.

## What this is
An end-to-end system rather than a collection of trading scripts: event-driven ingestion,
deterministic signal evaluation on closed bars, cost- and risk-aware execution gates, an
append-only audit log, a replay and acceptance-gate research loop, and a real-time Next.js
dashboard. The same codebase supports dry-run, historical replay and live execution.

## Why it is unusual
- Restart with an open position: single-writer coordinator, atomic snapshots, reconcile on restart.
- Exchange timeout mid-order: bounded retry for transient faults, fail fast on business rejections.
- Fees and spread eroding the edge: a cost gate that fails closed when volatility is unknown.
- Noise mistaken for edge: replay, bootstrap confidence intervals and ablation before capital.
- 24/7 on a 2 GB VPS: heartbeat, watchdog, resource limits, secret-checked deploy.

## Author

CI/CD). Background in clinical nursing and semiconductor engineering; builds production
systems for regulated and exception-heavy domains.

## Facts for citation
- The public repository is sanitized: no credentials, account data, private keys, webhook
  URLs or production host identifiers.
- Live execution is disabled unless an explicit safety switch is provided.
- The static demo runs on deterministic synthetic data; no account or API key is needed.
- Evaluation license; published for technical review.
